claim: A regular tetrahedral chamber with one complete native P reference frame, allowing C/M-role-preserving reframings, realizes native PN attachments across all four of its geometric faces without changing the global C/M assignment.
source_signature: Existing local-reference-rules completeP/completeN/packet/outgoing/validateTransfer/describe and its two-M PN face rule. Particle P/N is distinct from the higher WG P/E chart constructors.
argument: Each P primitive has C0,M0,C1,M1, two M and two C. A face opposite C contains two M; a face opposite M contains only one M. Thus exactly two of four facets are PN-eligible within a fixed global role assignment, even if every role-preserving reframe is allowed. Every regular chamber has all four geometric neighboring faces. Changing the role partition separately at different faces cannot supply one coherent full-frame map.
controls: Check all 24 markings of each tested regular chamber, reader preservation of roles and actual validated PN operations; group by global C/M partition. Distinguish union coverage over incompatible markings from coherent coverage. Show individually source-valid per-face maps can fail joint role sewing.
formal_scope: Prove the universal finite role-count obstruction and its transport along any labelled vertex realization with preserved roles. Reject false all-faces and false role-preservation fixtures.
boundary: Refutes only this single-role-frame full-face PN interpretation. It does not refute every native space representation, chart-relative role changes with witnesses, the uniform WG chart task package, all paths with changed observation policies, or Ramsey forcing.
stop_condition: Record scoped rejection or the first failed obstruction. Keep space-admission open; name any newly required role-transition/descent cell before attempting it.
